title: Thermal Quantum Sensing: Fisher Information and Work Beyond Gaussian Signals
authors: Yash Chitgopekar, Nikolaos Koukoulekidis, Iman Marvian
abstract: Understanding how thermal fluctuations modify or suppress quantum-enhanced sensing is a central problem in quantum metrology. Closely related questions arise in quantum thermodynamics, particularly regarding the relation between the work induced by a signal and the information acquired by a sensor. Here, we establish general relations among the sensitivity of thermal quantum states, as quantified by different quantum Fisher information metrics, their temperature dependence, and the work induced by a unitary signal. We further show that, at high temperature, all monotone QFI metrics coincide to leading order with a universal quantity that can be expressed as the variance of a simple observable and itself defines a lesser-known QFI metric. This emergent uniqueness is reminiscent of the uniqueness of classical Fisher information in information geometry. In continuous-variable systems, the infinite-temperature limit is finite and generically non-zero for quadratic Gaussian signals, while it diverges for higher-degree signals. Remarkably, for any purely quadratic signal generator, the infinite-temperature QFI is at least twice the zero-temperature SLD QFI or, equivalently, at least eight times the ground-state variance of the generator. Consequently, the Cramér--Rao lower bound on the estimator variance is reduced by at least a factor of two. We illustrate these results using harmonic chains of bosonic modes relevant to trapped-ion platforms and quantum field-theoretic models.
summary: This paper develops a theoretical framework to understand quantum sensing in the presence of thermal noise by relating sensing sensitivity (QFI) to the work done. It establishes universal high-temperature limits for various QFI metrics, providing quantitative bounds on how thermal fluctuations affect measurement precision in bosonic systems.
main_problem: The paper addresses how thermal fluctuations modify quantum-enhanced sensing and establishes general relationships between sensing sensitivity (QFI) and the work done by a signal in quantum thermodynamics.
main_result: At high temperatures, various QFI metrics converge to a universal quantity related to the variance of a simple observable, and for quadratic signals, the high-temperature QFI is bounded by the zero-temperature SLD QFI.
method: The authors establish general relations between different Quantum Fisher Information (QFI) metrics and the work done, analyzing the system's behavior in the high-temperature limit ($ eta 	o 0^+$).
model_or_system: The analysis uses thermal quantum states (Gibbs state $ho_ eta$) subjected to unitary signals $U(s)$. Specific models include 1D harmonic chains of bosonic modes relevant to trapped-ion platforms and continuous-variable Gaussian systems.
key_observables: Quantum Fisher Information metrics (SLD, RLD, BKM, IA), induced work $W(s)$, and the Purity of Coherence $P_A(ho_ eta)$.
important_parameters: Temperature ($T$ or $ eta$), signal strength ($s$), and coupling constants ($\kappa, g, f$).
main_assumptions: The analysis often relies on the high-temperature limit ($ eta 	o 0^+$) or the quadratic nature of the signal generator in continuous-variable systems.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the sensing protocol and plot various QFI metrics versus temperature, showing their convergence behavior. Tables summarize extremal Bohr frequencies ($\omega_{\pm}$) for different signal types.
paper_structure: The paper develops general relations connecting QFI metrics to work, analyzes the high-temperature limit for bosonic systems, and applies these concepts to specific models like harmonic chains using both uniform and single-site signal generators.
why_interesting: This work provides rigorous theoretical tools to quantify the fundamental limits of quantum sensing in realistic, noisy (thermal) environments, connecting metrology directly to quantum thermodynamics.
